title: Nilpotent adjoint operators detect nilpotent connected groups in characteristic zero
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], with algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $\mathfrak g=T_{G/k,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with commutator bracket [def-wf-lie-algebra]. The adjoint representation $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak g)$ is the differential of conjugation, and $\operatorname{ad}(X)(Y)=[X,Y]$. Assume $\operatorname{char}k=0$. If for every $X\in\mathfrak g$ there is an integer $m\geq1$ with $\operatorname{ad}(X)^m=0$, then $G$ is nilpotent: there are closed normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] $G=G_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_c=1$ such that, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, $g\in G(A)$, $h\in G_i(A)$ and $0\leq i<c$, one has $ghg^{-1}h^{-1}\in G_{i+1}(A)$. The trivial group and $\mathfrak g=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Proposition 17.80 proof, printed p.378, characteristic-zero exclusion, read with additive Jordan decomposition (17.74, p.377), Proposition 10.15 (p.190), and descending central series (6.38, p.133). This is an agent-stated intermediate criterion implicit in the exclusion, not a separately numbered assertion in Milne. Springer 1998, 13.3.5, cited there for details, is WANTED.

proof.text: By the adjoint-differential lemma, $\mathfrak g$ is finite-dimensional and $d\operatorname{Ad}_e=\operatorname{ad}$. Apply the Noetherian Engel criterion with $R=k$, $L=\mathfrak g$: every subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space is finitely generated. The hypothesis gives $C^d\mathfrak g=0$, where $C^0\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g$ and $C^{r+1}\mathfrak g=[\mathfrak g,C^r\mathfrak g]$. Increase $d$ if necessary so $d\geq1$.

Put $V=\mathfrak g$ and $J=\{u\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):u(C^rV)\subseteq C^{r+1}V\text{ for }0\leq r<d\}$. It is a linear subspace closed under composition: two lowering maps lower twice, and $C^{r+2}V\subseteq C^{r+1}V$. A product of $d$ lowering maps kills $V$, so $J^d=0$. Here $J^i$ is the linear span of products of $i$ elements of $J$. For every $k$-algebra $A$ set $U_i(A)=1+(J^i\otimes_k A)$ for $1\leq i\leq d$. These are closed subgroup schemes of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$: the affine translates of the linear subspaces $J^i$ consist of units, with inverse $(1+u)^{-1}=1-u+\cdots+(-u)^{d-1}$, and are closed in the open scheme $\operatorname{GL}(V)\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V)$. Their multiplication and inverse are these polynomial formulas. Thus $U_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_d=1$, and the dual-number formula $1+\epsilon u$ gives $\operatorname{Lie}(U_1)=J$.

source.place: Agent construction from the central-series definition, 14.34, and polynomial matrix multiplication.

proof.text: For $X\in\mathfrak g$, the definition of $C^{r+1}V$ gives $\operatorname{ad}(X)(C^rV)\subseteq C^{r+1}V$. Hence $d\operatorname{Ad}_e(\mathfrak g)\subseteq J=\operatorname{Lie}(U_1)$. Apply Lie-detected factorization to $\operatorname{Ad}:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ and the closed subgroup $U_1$. Its source is smooth and connected by hypothesis, and the base field has characteristic zero. We obtain a group-scheme homomorphism $\rho:G\to U_1$ whose composite with the inclusion is $\operatorname{Ad}$.

source.place: 10.14-10.15 and Cartier 3.23; apply to the inverse image of U_1.

proof.text: All following identities hold over any commutative $k$-algebra $A$. If $s=1+u\in U_1(A)$ and $t=1+v\in U_i(A)$, then $uv-vu\in J^{i+1}\otimes_k A$, and $sts^{-1}t^{-1}-1=(st-ts)s^{-1}t^{-1}=(uv-vu)s^{-1}t^{-1}$. Multiplication on either side by the finite inverse polynomials in $u,v$ preserves $J^{i+1}\otimes_k A$, because $J^{i+1}$ is a two-sided ideal in the unital algebra $k\cdot1+J$. Thus $[U_1(A),U_i(A)]\subseteq U_{i+1}(A)$ for $i<d$. This also proves $U_i$ normal in $U_1$, and $U_d=1$ is normal as well.

source.place: Agent matrix calculation realizing the descending central series in 6.38, printed p.133.

proof.text: Define $G_i=G\times_{U_1}U_{i+1}$ for $0\leq i<d$ and append $G_d=1$. Pulling back the closed normal inclusions gives closed normal subgroup schemes of $G$, and $G_0=G$. The calculation in the preceding step gives $[G(A),G_i(A)]\subseteq G_{i+1}(A)$ for $i<d-1$. Finally $G_{d-1}=\ker\rho=\ker\operatorname{Ad}$, since $U_d=1$ and $U_1\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is a monomorphism. The adjoint-kernel lemma says that this subgroup commutes with $G(A)$ for every $A$, proving the last required inclusion into $G_d(A)=\{1\}$. These polynomial constructions work also for $V=0$ (then $J=0$ and $U_1=1$), and for the trivial group.
